title: Spring Nino 3.4 change cut warm-threshold probability error against a level model in 1982-2026 winters
abstract: We tested whether MAM minus DJF Nino 3.4 improves next-DJF probabilities of an anomaly at or above 1.5 C. Each fit used earlier years from 1951. Student t tails from linear models gave 45 tests for winters 1982-2026, with six events. Adding change cut Brier error from 0.125629 to 0.104144, a 17.10% gain against spring level alone. The conditional 95% five-year block interval was 3.51% to 30.51%. Against earlier-year event frequency, the gain was 12.54%, with limits -4.65% to 28.47%. Trend adjustment and removal of three large warm winters also left uncertain gains against the level model. Thus, evidence depends on the baseline and sample. This extends a prior mean-score test to a probability score in an overlapping record. Few events, revised SST data, simple tail rules and conditional intervals limit inference. The result does not establish calibration, physical cause or operational skill. Source bytes, code, forecasts, scores, uncertainty draws, a figure and numerical checks are included.
